titulo: Your AC doesn't make cold air ❄️ #howitworks #shorts
descripcion:
An air conditioner never brings cold air in. It grabs the heat in your room and throws it outside, with the same trick your fridge uses.

lineas.texto: Your air conditioner doesn't pull cold air in from outside.
It grabs the heat inside your room, and throws it outside.
Warm room air gets sucked through a coil full of freezing cold fluid.
The coil soaks up the heat, and a fan blows the cooled air back into your room.
That's also why it drips. Water in the air condenses on the cold coil, like on a cold soda can.
The fluid carries all that heat outside, through these two pipes.
Out there, a compressor squeezes it until it's even hotter than a summer day.
So a big fan blows the heat away. That's the hot air you feel next to the outdoor unit.
Then the fluid expands, turns ice cold again, and flows back in for more. Same trick as your fridge.
